answers.explanation: ALB is Layer 7 — path/host rules, WAF (REGIONAL), and authenticate-oidc/cognito actions. NLB/GWLB cannot do HTTP routing or WAF at L7.
NLB provides static IP/EIP per AZ and TCP passthrough so instances terminate TLS. ALB would terminate TLS unless configured for passthrough (TLS listener to TLS target).
GWLB is for inline third-party appliances (firewalls/IDS) using GENEVE. ALB/NLB distribute to app targets, not inspection fleets.
Health check uses port 8080 but instance SG only allows 443 — checks fail while manual curl on 8080 works from bastion. Allow ALB SG → target port 8080 (health check port must match SG).
HealthCheckGracePeriod suspends ASG health checks (including ELB) while instances boot. Deregistration delay is for scale-in draining, not launch.
Failover routing requires health checks on the primary (or associated child checks). Without them Route 53 keeps sending traffic to a failed primary.
NLB supports UDP (and TCP/TLS) at Layer 4. ALB is HTTP/HTTPS/WebSockets — not raw UDP telemetry.
Deregistration delay (connection draining) lets in-flight requests complete when a target is deregistered during scale-in or deploy.
Standard three-tier pattern: ALB SG allows client ingress; task SG allows app port only from ALB SG. Matches Night 9 Fargate SG thinking (least privilege).
ALB cross-zone ON by default; NLB cross-zone OFF by default. Disabling NLB cross-zone reduces cross-AZ transfer when clients hit NLB nodes in their own AZ.
TCP health check only verifies port open, not HTTP semantics. If app needs GET /ping, use HTTP/HTTPS health check with that path.
ALB supports Lambda as a target type with listener rules. NLB cannot invoke Lambda as an L7 target in the same way.
ALB is a managed multi-AZ service — DNS resolves to nodes in healthy AZs. Individual target failures are handled by health checks, not whole-AZ ALB failure.
ALB duration-based stickiness sets AWSALB cookie so sessions hit the same target. NLB has 5-tuple stickiness for TCP flows, not HTTP session cookies.
GWLB endpoints in VPC subnets redirect traffic to the GWLB for inspection through appliances. Not IGW or ALB.
HTTPS listener → HTTP target is TLS termination (SSL offloading) at ALB. Passthrough would forward encrypted bytes unchanged (NLB TCP or ALB TLS→TLS).
ASG health check type ELB uses target group health status to mark instances InService or terminate unhealthy ones.
NLB EIPs give stable IPs for partner allowlists while targets scale behind them. ALB DNS name is stable but IP set changes — partners often require fixed IPs.
WAF on ALB uses REGIONAL scope in the ALB Region. CLOUDFRONT scope is only for CloudFront distributions (Night 4/6/7 WAF scope questions).

502 from ALB often means LB could not connect to target — wrong target port in TG registration vs process listen port is a classic post-deploy miss. Health check can pass on a different port/path than traffic.
